questions.solution:
$Given,

$f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $f\left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{m}}\left\{\sqrt{2} \left($\sin x - \cos x\right) + m - 2\right\}$, for some $m$,

Also given~the range of $f$ is \left[0, 2\right]$,

Now we know that,

$- $\sqrt{2} \lesinx -$\cos x \le $\sqrt{2}

$⇒ - 2 \le $\sqrt{2}\left($\sin x - \cos x\right) ≤ 2$

(Assuming~\sqrt{2} \left(\sin x - \cos x\right) = k$)

$⇒ - 2 \le k \le 2 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now taking function~$f \left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{m}} \left($k + m - 2\right)$

Given,~$0 $\$lef\left(x\right) ≤ 2$

$⇒ 0 \le \log_{\mathrm{m}} \left(k + m - 2\right) ≤ 2$

$⇒ 1 ≤ k + m - 2 ≤ m$

$⇒ - m + 3 ≤ k ≤ 2 \ldots \left(2\right)$

Now from equations \left($1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$- m + 3 = - 2$

$⇒ m = 5$

questions.solution:
$

Given that& $f\left(x\right) = \log \left($4x^{2} + 11x + 6\right) + \sin^{- 1}\left($4x + 3\right) + \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{10x + 6}{3}\right)

We know that the domain of~$A \left(x\right) + B \left(x\right) + C \left($x\right)$~is~$D \left($A\right) \cap D \left($B\right) \cap D \left(C\right)$.

Let us find the domain of~$\log \left(4x^{2} + 11x + 6\right)$.

We know that domain of~$\log \left(f \left(x\right)\right)$~is~$f\left(x\right) > 0$.

$⇒ 4x^{2} + 11x + 6 > 0$

$⇒ 4x^{2} + 8x + 3x + 6 > 0$

$⇒ \left(4x + 3\right) \left($x + 2\right) > 0$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \infty , -$2\right) \cup $\left(\dfrac{- 3}{4}, \infty)$

Domain of~$\log \left($4x^{2} + 11x + 9\right)$~is~$x \in \left(- \infty , -2\right) \cup \left(\dfrac{- 3}{4}, \infty\right).

Let us find the domain of~$\sin^{- 1} \left(4x + 3\right)$

$⇒ - 1 ≤ 4x + 3 ≤ 1$

$⇒ - 1 ≤ x \le \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$⇒ x \in \left[-$1, $\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right]

Let us find the domain of~$\cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{10x + 6}{3}\right).$

$⇒ - 1 \le \dfrac{10x + 6}{3} \le1$

$⇒ - 3 ≤ 10x + 6 ≤ 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 9}{10} \lex \le \dfrac{- 3}{10}.$

Now the common domain is~$\dfrac{- 3}{4} \lex \le \dfrac{- 1}{2}.$

$⇒ x \in \left[\dfrac{- 3}{4}, \dfrac{- 1}{2}\right]$

But given that the domain of~$f \left($x\right)$~is~$x \in \left[\alpha, \beta\right].$

$⇒ \alpha = $\dfrac{- 3}{4}, \beta = \dfrac{- 1}{2}.

$⇒ \left|36\left(\alpha + \beta\right)\right| = \left|36\left(\dfrac{- 3}{4} + \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)\right)|

$⇒ \left|36\left(\alpha + \beta\right)\right| = \left|36 \times $\dfrac{- 5}{4}\right|

$⇒ \left|36\left(\alpha + \beta\right)\right| =45$

Therefore, the required answer is~$45$.

$

questions.q: Let $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}f\left(a + k\right) = 16\left({2}^{10} - 1\right),$ where the function $f$ satisfies $f \left(x + y\right) = f  \left($x\right)f \left(y\right)$ for all natural numbers $x, y$ and $f\left(1\right) = 2 .$ Then the natural number $'a'$ is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f \left(1\right) = 2$~and~$f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right)\$cdotf\left($y\right)$

Put $x = y = 1$

$⇒ $f\left($2\right) = $f\left($1\right) \cdotf\left(1\right) = {2}^{2}$

Now, put~$x = 1, y = 2$

$⇒ f\left(3\right) = f\left(1\right) \$cdotf\left($2\right) = {2}^{3}$

Now, put~$x = 1, y = 3$

$⇒ $f\left($4\right) = $f\left($1\right) \cdotf\left(3\right) = {2}^{4}$

Similarly, $f\left(10\right) = {2}^{10}$

Now $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}f \left(a + k\right) = 16 \left({2}^{10} -1\right)$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}f \left($a\right)f \left($k\right) = 16 \left({2}^{10} -1\right)$

$⇒ f \left($a\right)\mathop{∑}_{k = $1}^{10}f\left($k\right) = $16\left({2}^{10} -$1\right)$

$⇒ f \left($a\right) \left($f \left($1\right) + $f\left($2\right) \ldots + $f\left($10\right)\right) = $16\left({2}^{10} -$1\right)$

$⇒ f \left($a\right)\left({2}^{1} + {2}^{2} + {2}^{3} + \ldots + {2}^{10}\right) = 16\left({2}^{10} - 1\right)$

Using the sum of~$n$~terms of a geometric progression, i.e.~$a + ar + ar^{2} + ar^{3} + . . . + ar^{n - 1} = $\dfrac{a \left(r^{n} - 1\right)}$${r - 1},$~we get

$f \left(a\right)\dfrac{2 \left({2}^{10} -1\right)}{2 - 1} =16\left({2}^{10} -1\right)$

$⇒ f\left(a\right) = 8 = {2}^{3}$

Also, we know that~$f \left(3\right) = 8$

$⇒ f\left(a\right) = f\left(3\right)$

$⇒ a = 3 .$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\}$. Then the number of elements in the set {f: S \times S \to S: f$~is onto and $f \left(a, b\right) = f  \left($b, a\right)$~$\gea \forall  \left(a, b\right) \in S \timesS}& is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Finding the cases for& $f\left(a, b\right) = f\left(b, a\right) \ge a$~we have,

\left(1, 1\right), \left(1, 4\right), \left($4, 1\right), \left(2, 4\right), \left(4, 2\right), \left(3, 4\right), \left(4, 3\right), \left(4, 4\right)$- all have one choice for image.

\left(2, 1\right), \left(1, 2\right), \left(2, 2\right) -$~all have three choices for image.

\left(3, 2\right), \left(2, 3\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(1, 3\right), \left(3, 3\right) -$all have two choices for image.

So the total functions~$= 3 \times3 \times2 \times2 \times2 = 72$

Case 1: None of the pre-images have~$3$~as image.~

Total functions~$= 2 \times2 \times1 \times1 \times1 = 4$

Case 2: None of the pre-images have~$2$~as image

Total functions~$= 2 \times2 \times2 \times2 \times2 = 32$

Case 3: None of the pre-images have either~$3$~or~$2$~as image

Total functions~$= 1 \times1 \times1 \times1 \times1 = 1$

$∴$~Total onto functions~$= 72 - 4 - 32 + 1 = 37

$

questions.q: Suppose a differentiable function& $f  \left(x\right)$ satisfies the identity~$f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + f\left(y\right) + xy^{2} + x^{2}y,$~for all real $x$ and $y$. If~$\lim_{x \to 0}$\dfrac{f  \left(x\right)}{x} =$1,$~then~$f^{'}\left($3\right) is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∵ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x} = 1 ⇒ f ' \left(0\right) = 1$

$f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + f\left(y\right) + xy^{2} + x^{2}y$

Differentiate w.r.t.~$x$~keeping~$y$~constant

$f ' \left(x + y\right) = f ' \left(x\right) + 0 + y^{2} + 2xy$

put~$y = - x$

$f ' \left(0\right) = f ' \left(x\right) + x^{2} - 2x^{2}$

$1 = f ' \left(x\right) - x^{2}$

$f ' \left(x\right) = 1 + x^{2}$

$f ' \left(3\right) = 10$.

questions.q: If the range of $f(\theta)=\frac{\sin ^4 \theta+3 \cos ^2 \theta}{\sin ^4 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta}, \theta \in \mathbb{R}$ is $[\alpha, \beta]$, then the sum of the infinite G.P., whose first term is 64 and the common ratio is $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$, is equal to________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(\theta)=\frac{\sin ^4 \theta+3 \cos ^2 \theta}{\sin ^4 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta} \\ & f(\theta)=1+\frac{2 \cos ^2 \theta}{\sin ^4 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta} \\ & f(\theta)=\frac{2 \cos ^2 \theta}{\cos ^4 \theta-\cos ^2 \theta+1}+1 \\ & f(\theta)=\frac{2}{\cos ^2 \theta+\sec ^2 \theta-1}+1 \\ & \left.f(\theta)\right|_{\text {min. }}=1 \\ & f(\theta)_{\text {max. }}=3 \\ & S=\frac{64}{1-1 / 3}=96\end{aligned}$
